public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1009

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1009](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1009)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97--109.
- [Gy88] Győri, E., *On the number of edge-disjoint triangles in graphs of given size*. (1988),
  267--276.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1009

/--
Is it true that, for every $c>0$, there exists $f(c)$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices with
at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges, where $k<c n$, contains at least $k-f(c)$ many edge
disjoint triangles?

Erdős [Er71] proved this for $c<1/2$ using a theorem of Erdős and Gallai, which says that every
graph on $n$ vertices with at least $(n-1)^2/4+2$ many edges, with chromatic number $3$, must
contain a triangle. In fact, Erdős proved this is true with $f(c)=0$ for $c<1/2$. At first Erdős
thought $f(c)=0$ for larger values of $c$ but this is false: an example of Sauer proves that
$f(2)\geq 1$.

This is true, and was proved by Győri [Gy88] who proved that this is true with $f(c)\ll c^2$,
and also that $f(c)=0$ if $c<2$ for odd $n$ or $c<3/2$ for even $n$.

A family of edge disjoint triangles is a finite set of $3$-cliques of $G$ any two of which share
at most one vertex.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1009.lean#L2347"]
theorem erdos_1009 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ f : ℕ, ∀ (n k : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    n ^ 2 / 4 + k ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard → (k : ℝ) < c * n →
      ∃ T : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
        (T : Set (Finset (Fin n))).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ k ≤ T.card + f := by
  sorry

/--
Sauer gave an example of a graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+2n-6$ many edges
which contains only $2n-7$ many edge disjoint triangles: if $n=2r+4$ then $G$ is the complete
tripartite graph on $[r]\times [r]\times [4]$, with a $K_4$ on the $[4]$ vertices also.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1009.variants.sauer : ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * r + 4)),
    G.edgeSet.ncard = (2 * r + 4) ^ 2 / 4 + 2 * (2 * r + 4) - 6 ∧
      ∀ T : Finset (Finset (Fin (2 * r + 4))), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) →
        (T : Set (Finset (Fin (2 * r + 4)))).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) →
          T.card ≤ 2 * (2 * r + 4) - 7 := by
  sorry

end Erdos1009

findings.description: The historical paragraph says that Győri obtained f(c)=0 for c<2 when n is odd, or c<3/2 when n is even, without qualifying that n must be sufficiently large depending on c. Under the all-n interpretation of f(c) in the preceding problem statement, this is false: take c=1, n=4, k=2 and G=K₄. There are floor(n²/4)+k=6 edges and k<cn, but no two edge-disjoint triangles. This counterexample was checked in Lean. The main Lean proposition correctly permits a nonzero error term; neither formal theorem needs changing. The same abbreviated wording occurs on the cited problem page.
findings.source_evidence: Balogh–Wigal, Packing edge disjoint cliques in graphs, arXiv:2502.16683v2, “Concluding remarks” (linked from the discussion of https://www.erdosproblems.com/1009), gives the precise Győri ranges: k≤2n−10 for odd n and k≤1.5n−5 for even n. These imply the stated c-thresholds for sufficiently large n, not uniformly over all n.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the historical refinement as having no error term for sufficiently large n depending on c, or state the precise bounds k≤2n−10 and k≤3n/2−5. Leave both Lean theorem statements unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a natural-number error bound and the subtraction-free inequality k≤T.card+f. It represents edge-disjoint triangles by 3-cliques whose vertex-set intersections have cardinality at most one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any real error bound depending only on c can be enlarged to a natural number, and a natural bound is also a real bound. For natural cardinalities, k≤T.card+f is equivalent to (k:ℝ)−f≤T.card, including k<f. Two triangles share an edge exactly when they share two distinct vertices. Natural division n²/4 equals the required floor. A full equivalence with these more literal source formulations was proved as main_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No misformalization was found in either Lean proposition. The linked external proof and its dependencies rebuilt successfully; both its theorem and a bridge to the exact reviewed proposition depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Sauer’s construction and bounds agree with Erdős’s original p. 98: it has r²+8r+6 edges, at most 4r packing triangles meeting the two r-vertex parts, and at most one wholly inside the K₄. Small edge counts and boundary cases were checked in Lean. The original Gy88 chapter was not obtainable; its results were cross-checked through the problem page, its mathematical discussion, and Balogh–Wigal. All experiments stayed under /workspace/review; the reviewed file is unchanged.
